title: Extropian CAE Workbench
description: A desktop workbench for unified CAE — open and inspect models, manipulate them with gizmos, configure and run solver studies, and extend with custom gizmos, solver configs, and workflows.
tagline: One desktop platform for unified CAE — import, model, solve, and visualize, extended by you.
capabilities: Unified CAE host: open, inspect (model tree + inspector), and manipulate models with gizmos in a 3D viewport
Schema-driven solver run configuration on a worker thread with live, per-stamp post-processing
Parallel, deterministic design studies over real solver physics
JSON command surface + `wb` shim for automation from any language, workflow recipes, in-process Lua, and MCP agents
Extension API for custom gizmos, solver backends, and styles; savable JSON project state
foundation: Mirrors and consumes the Extropian ecosystem: exd::cae, exd::render, exd::physics, exd::geometry, exd::viz, exd::optimization, exd::spatial-ui, exd::mcp
CommandBus/EventBus platform nervous system over an ECS core (exd::core)
Panels staged on extropian-spatial-ui (Dear ImGui retired); UI-agnostic content dumps underneath
body:
The Extropian CAE Workbench is the platform product of the Extropian ecosystem: a desktop app where an engineer opens a model from the unified CAE IR (machine recipes, or OBJ/STL/Gmsh adapters), inspects it in a model tree and inspector, manipulates parts with gizmos in a full-window 3D viewport, and configures a solver run from typed schemas. Solver work runs on a worker thread with live post-processing — velocity and pressure fields streamed from the running solver rebuild slices, streamlines, and particle clouds every stamp, and parallel design studies optimize over real variables.

Architecturally it is the `exd::workbench` library plus one reference app. Every user action is a command on a CommandBus (named and undoable); cross-system notifications are typed events on an EventBus; panels read ECS state, dispatch commands, and subscribe to events. The UI is staged on Extropian Spatial UI widget trees with UI-agnostic content dumps underneath, so panels can re-render elsewhere without touching services. Everything consumes — never reimplements — the ecosystem mirror (extropian-cae, render, physics, geometry, viz, optimization, spatial-ui, mcp).

Extensibility and automation are first-class platform promises. Users register custom gizmos, solver backends, and styles against an unconditional extension API; a JSON command surface (socket/CLI/event-stream, plus a tiny `wb` shim) lets researchers drive the workbench from any language; workflow recipes orchestrate multi-step studies; in-process Lua covers interactive niches; and AI agents talk to the same surface via extropian-mcp.

title: Extropian Synthesis
description: Generative AI and optimization platform for synthesizing novel machines from known physics, geometry, and materials — Extropian Synthesis.
tagline: A generative AI and optimization powered platform for synthesizing known laws of nature, geometries, materials, and computational algorithms to invent novel machines at any scale.
capabilities: Generative synthesis grounded in known laws of nature rather than free-form generation
Combines physics, geometry, materials, and computational algorithms in one design loop
Optimization-driven exploration of machine concepts across scales
Built on the Extropian simulation and geometry foundations
foundation: Research-stage platform (direction of travel for the ecosystem's AI work)
Draws on Extropian Physics, Extropian Geometry, and Extropian Optimization
Designed to output designs that existing solvers can validate
body:
Extropian Synthesis is the ecosystem's generative design platform: instead of generating imagery or text, it synthesizes *machines* — combining known laws of nature, geometries, materials, and computational algorithms to invent novel designs at any scale.

The premise is that generated concepts are only useful when they can be simulated and validated. Synthesis is being built on the Extropian simulation stack so that every proposed design is checkable against real physics.

title: Extropian Spatial UI
description: 2D/2.5D UI rendered directly inside any GL context — widgets as ordinary ECS entities in the same scene graph as 3D geometry. No DOM, no document runtime.
tagline: 2.5D UI as ECS entities in your GL scene — widgets, layout, and interaction, no DOM.
capabilities: Widgets as ordinary ECS entities in one scene graph with 3D geometry
Deterministic dirty-driven pipeline: size, flex layout, mesh, interaction
Pure-math layout — Column/Row/Absolute plus a built-in flex engine
Rich widget catalog: controls, containers, charts, diagrams, and LLM-authored JSON schema
Headless-first and WASM-safe: null-window tests, injected mesh creation, screenshot capture
foundation: Pure ECS + SceneGraph from extropian-core, text and meshes from extropian-geometry, GL rendering via extropian-render, window/input from extropian-app
FreeType SDF glyph atlas and HarfBuzz-driven text pipeline
CPU-side mesh generation only — no GPU, DOM, or document runtime in the library
body:
Most engineering software lives with a split personality: a native or DOM-based UI bolted onto a graphics engine. Extropian Spatial UI eliminates that divide by rendering 2D/2.5D UI directly inside the GL context. Widgets — panels, buttons, labels, headers, separators — are ordinary spatial entities living in the same `ecs::Registry` and `ecs::SceneGraph` as 3D geometry, CAE models, and data visualizations. There is no separate 2D scene, no DOM, and no document runtime.

Resolution runs as a deterministic dirty-tag pipeline: a font/viewport structural phase, a layout phase where Column/Row/Absolute containers reflow through a pure-math flex engine, then a mesh-generation and interaction phase that uploads meshes and assigns stable pick IDs. The library never touches the GPU — meshes are uploaded through an injected mesh-create function into the Extropian Render graphics context, while hit resolution and event dispatch (hover/click/drag, keyboard focus, scroll, selection) stay in this library.

The system is headless-first and WASM-safe: every stage runs with a null window and an injected mesh callback, verified by a headless doctest suite and scriptable screenshot capture. The widget catalog spans controls, containers, charts and data-viz, and diagram widgets — including widgets authored from an LLM-style JSON schema via the semantic builder.

title: Extropian Render
description: A modular, ECS-based 3D rendering framework for the Extropian ecosystem — multi-pass scenes, built-in cameras, picking, and a 3D transform gizmo.
tagline: Modular ECS rendering engine for the Extropian ecosystem — PBR, NPR, particles, volume, and built-in interaction.
capabilities: Multi-pass ECS-driven rendering: sky, opaque, PBR, NPR, particles, volume, highlights, and a 2D UI overlay
Default hot-reloadable shader library: Lambert/Phong, PBR metallic-roughness with IBL, and four NPR styles
Unified camera system — FPS, orbit, walk, and ortho-2D modes with runtime FOV
Built-in interaction: CPU raycast picking, GPU ID-buffer picking, hover/selection highlighting, and a 3D transform gizmo
GPU resource managers with instanced draw-call batching and external mesh import (OBJ/STL/FBX/STEP)
foundation: Built on extropian-core (ECS, math, SceneGraph) and extropian-app (window, input, OpenGL context)
Systems scheduled by core::SystemGraph; renderer owns no registry, no UI semantics
IRenderer abstraction across OpenGL 4.6, WebGL 2.0, headless Null, and a committed Vulkan slot
body:
Extropian Render is the rendering backend of the ecosystem: a reusable, ECS-based 3D rendering framework that consumes plain ECS entities and draws them through a multi-pass pipeline. It depends only on extropian-core and extropian-app, and treats everything submitted as ECS state identically — direct scene entities, external models, or spatial-ui widgets — with no UI, app, or orchestration coupling.

A platform-agnostic RenderSystem drives passes for sky, opaque, Phong, PBR, four NPR styles, reflective, transparent, particles, volume ray-march, highlight, gizmo overlay, and a 2D orthographic UI layer. GPU resource managers handle upload, hot-reloadable shaders, and instanced draw-call batching, while an `IRenderer` interface targets OpenGL 4.6 today with WebGL 2.0 and Vulkan as committed targets.

Built-in tooling supports scientific and engineering visualization: a unified camera (FPS/orbit/walk/ortho-2D with runtime FOV), CPU raycast and GPU ID-buffer picking, hover/selection highlighting, and a 3D transform gizmo. Default shaders include PBR metallic-roughness with optional IBL and NPR cel/technical/hatch/blueprint styles; meshes import from OBJ, STL, FBX, and STEP with optional diffuse textures.

title: Extropian Geometry
description: A renderer-independent parametric geometry engine — deterministic 2D and 3D meshing from structured descriptors, with construction operators, mesh processing, and interaction gizmos.
tagline: Geometry as a foundation, not an add-on — deterministic parametric 2D/3D meshing, renderer-independent by design.
capabilities: Deterministic 2D and 3D primitive mesh generation from immutable descriptors
Construction operators: extrusion, lathe, helix, loft/skin, SDF blending, terrain, deformation and FFD cages
Mesh processing: merge, transform, weld, normal recomputation, triangulation, exact CSG booleans, watertight gate
SVG-like Path2D fills/strokes, FreeType/HarfBuzz text shaping, glyph and SDF font atlases
Per-part transform and deform gizmos with a pure, headless-testable edit kernel
foundation: Depends only on extropian-core for math and mesh types; pure CPU math, no GPU, no ECS
Compiles to WASM with zero changes; tiered static library targets (2d, 3d, model, io, text, noise)
Designed as a layered kernel: geometry kernel → construction operators → domain recipes
body:
Extropian Geometry is a pure computational C++23 library: describe a shape with a structured descriptor, call a `generate_*_mesh()` function, get back deterministic `MeshData`. It covers a wide set of 2D primitives (rect, circle, arc, ring, star, grid, regular polygon, …) and 3D primitives (sphere, box, cylinder, torus, cone, tube, capsule, icosahedron, …), an SVG-like `Path2D` system, and extended construction — extrusion, lathe, helix, loft/skin between sections, heightmap/terrain, SDF blending via marching cubes, and bend/twist/taper/noise deformation plus FFD lattice cages. Mesh ops include merge, transform, welding, normal recomputation, concave polygon triangulation with holes, exact CSG booleans, and a watertight/closed-manifold gate.

The architecture is layered: a generic geometry kernel (profiles, paths, parametric surfaces, scalar fields, lofts, tessellation), construction operators (extrude, revolve, sweep, loft, implicit-field extraction, deform), and domain recipes built on top. It stays deliberately renderer-independent — no GPU, no ECS, only extropian-core for math/mesh types — and compiles to WASM with zero changes. Text shaping (FreeType + HarfBuzz glyph meshing, SDF font atlases) and per-part interaction gizmos (TRS plus bend/twist/taper/lattice) are included, with a pure, headless-testable edit kernel for parametric and direct editing.

The CAD/CAE model layer (parts, patches, materials, boundary conditions, format adapters, mass properties, machine recipes) now lives in the sibling extropian-cae, which builds on this library and relies on its documented face-ordering contracts. Geometry is pure shape generation again.

title: Extropian CAE
description: A modular C++ library built around CAEModel — a unified, format-agnostic in-memory representation of any multiphysics problem, with deterministic file-format adapters and two import/export tiers.
tagline: One model for any multiphysics problem — geometry, motion, loads, and analysis state, format-agnostic.
capabilities: Unified CAEModel IR spanning geometry, patches, materials, multiphysics topology, loads, motion, and analysis state
Deterministic adapters for STL, OBJ, Gmsh .msh, VTK/VTU, faceted STEP, MJCF, and URDF
Dependency-free WASM-clean importers, plus an optional OpenCASCADE/Assimp tier for STEP, IGES, BREP, FBX, glTF, 3DS, and more
Motion graph with fixed/revolute/continuous/prismatic joints, limits and compliance, and gear/belt/rack couplings
Mass properties and parametric machine recipes producing watertight, patched assemblies
foundation: Built on extropian-core math/mesh types and extropian-geometry mesh generation
Dependency-free core library with heavy deps isolated in the opt-in exd-cae-io module
Designed for solver intake: capability negotiation, content hashes, and deterministic validation
body:
Extropian CAE is the ecosystem's data foundation: a modular, dependency-light C++ library organized around **CAEModel**, a unified, format-agnostic in-memory IR. One model per part or machine carries everything an analysis needs: parts and assemblies with labelled CAE patches, a deterministic material database, multiphysics regions/domains/interfaces, physics-tagged boundary conditions and body loads, symmetry/cyclic/rotating frames, a motion graph of joints and couplings, and the analysis state itself — volume discretization, initial and ambient conditions, time domain, and physics couplings.

Every file format is an adapter over the model. Deterministic exporters cover OBJ, STL, Gmsh .msh, VTK/VTU, faceted STEP, and MJCF/URDF for mechanisms; importers rebuild CAEModel from OBJ, STL, Gmsh, FBX, and analytic STEP in a WASM-clean, dependency-free core. An opt-in tier (`exd-cae-io`) adds analytic STEP/IGES/BREP via OpenCASCADE and the wider mesh zoo (FBX/glTF/3DS/COLLADA/…) plus glTF 2.0 export via Assimp, with dependencies fetched automatically — no OS configuration required.

Parametric machine recipes (turbine, compressor, single-cylinder steam engine) return patched assemblies with mechanisms; full demo analysis scenes — from a ~2 m turbofan down to a µm-scale MEMS biosensor — populate every field and pass `validate_analysis()` with zero errors. Mass properties come from Mirtich tetrahedron decomposition.

title: Extropian Viz
description: Turns solver output into insight — slices, iso-surfaces, streamlines, particles, derived fields, and tensor glyphs from scalar, vector, and tensor fields.
tagline: Post-process solver output into insight — slices, iso-surfaces, streamlines, glyphs, and derived fields.
capabilities: Slice planes + scientific colormaps (grayscale, hot, jet, viridis, inferno, cool_warm) with auto-scaling from percentile stats
Watertight iso-surfaces (marching tets), streamlines (RK2/RK4, deterministic seeds), and particles
Field-on-mesh annotation: per-vertex coloring, plane cross-sections, iso-contour lines
Derived fields: gradient, curl, divergence, vorticity, Q-criterion
Tensor glyphs via Jacobi eigen-decomposition and fractional anisotropy, plus bounded-history point probes
foundation: Built on exd::core math/mesh types and generic solver-output fields, with no dependency on a solver
Planned GPU path behind a ComputeBackend, borrowing Extropian Render's shared GL context
Headless-testable CPU reference cores with analytic references and _into reuse for real-time use
body:
Solver output is only valuable when it can be seen, compared, and understood. Extropian Viz (`exd::viz`) is a generic scientific-field visualization library that consumes scalar/vector/tensor fields on uniform grids (`UniformGrid`, `Field3D<T>`) and produces the core post-processing and visualization techniques: slice planes with transfer-function colormapping, watertight iso-surfaces via marching tets, RK2/RK4 streamlines, particles, bounded-history point probes, tensor glyphs (Jacobi eigen-decomposition, fractional anisotropy), and derived fields (gradient, curl, divergence, vorticity, Q-criterion). Data maps onto existing geometry too — per-vertex field coloring, plane cross-sections, and iso-contour lines on meshes — without ever rewriting topology.

Architecturally it is interface-first and GPU-behind-the-interface: every algorithm ships as a deterministic CPU reference implementation with analytic headless tests, and a `ComputeBackend` interface is planned so GPU kernels (slice extraction, iso compaction, particle advection, resampling) can arrive without touching the public API. The library depends on `exd::core` only and never on a solver or renderer; solver outputs and product data are adapted into viz inputs by consuming repos.

The optional showcase demo walks every landed technique on an analytic Taylor–Green vortex rendered through Extropian Render, and the planned ECS layer publishes render outputs so a host render pipeline draws them without knowing viz exists.

title: Extropian Physics
description: A modular multiphysics numerical engine — compose independent solvers (CFD, thermal, structural, electromagnetics, turbomachinery, and more) through a validated coupling engine, GPU-portable by design.
tagline: One composable runtime — couple physics, not solvers.
capabilities: Coupled multiphysics runs (FSI, conjugate heat transfer, thermal stress, joule heating, aeroacoustics, species-in-flow) via a validated coupling engine
FDM-based incompressible 3D CFD with immersed solids and Boussinesq natural convection
Grid-first solvers: thermal, structural elasticity, acoustics, particles, chemistry, porous media, electromagnetics, species transport
Axial mean-line turbomachinery (stages, operating maps, Greitzer surge) and reduced-order BEM turbines
Rotating-machine presets: coupled turbines, Otto-cycle combustion and Rankine-lite steam engines with governors and generator loads
Deterministic, batchable entry points with real-time field/CSV output channels
foundation: Composable runtime abstraction: data, operators, physics, discretization, coupling, execution, hardware
Fidelity profiles from REALTIME to HIGH_FIDELITY across the same configurations
No-exceptions design (ModelStatus) with typed config/result contracts, verified by analytic-anchored unit tests
body:
Extropian Physics is the numerical heart of the ecosystem: a single composable numerical engine, not a collection of monolithic solvers. It builds simulations from data + operators + physics + discretization + coupling + execution + hardware: physics modules declare mathematical requirements, a coupling engine links them over typed field channels with validated contracts (units, rank, conservation, temporal behavior), and presets assemble verified configurations — coupled wind/water turbines, Otto-cycle and steam engines, incompressible 3D FDM CFD, conjugate heat transfer, aeroacoustics, and more. It runs CPU today (parallel_for/reduce/stencil primitives) behind a hardware-independent design that targets a CUDA GPU backend.

The solver cores are real and analytic-verified: FDM stencil operators (gradient/divergence/curl/Laplacian/advection), matrix-free linear solvers (CG/GMRES/BiCGSTAB), eight ODE integrators, and grid-first domains including thermal, acoustics, linear elasticity, particles, chemistry, porous media, and species transport. Turbomachinery covers axial mean-line stages and stacks (compressor/turbine senses emerge from geometry), operating maps, and Greitzer surge dynamics. A deterministic import pipeline turns external CAE models into solver-ready meshes and materials; output streams binary field stamps and CSV machine-state series at a real-time cadence for visualization and optimization loops.

Because the engine is modular, an engagement rarely adopts it whole — more often a solver, a coupling strategy, or the execution layer becomes the starting point for a specialized application.

title: Extropian Optimization
description: A domain-independent optimization library for black-box engineering design spaces — five pluggable algorithms, deterministic reproducible runs, constraint handling, and a steppable embedding API.
tagline: Deterministic, embeddable optimization engine for black-box engineering design spaces.
capabilities: Five pluggable algorithms: CMA-ES, NSGA-II, Nelder-Mead, Hooke-Jeeves, differential evolution
Deterministic, bit-for-bit reproducible runs — invariant to thread count
Continuous, integer, and categorical variables with constraint handling (adaptive penalty, constrained domination)
Parallel batch evaluation via an index-ordered thread pool
Steppable embedding API for hosts that own their evaluation pipeline, plus JSON-defined problems
foundation: Built for the Extropian ecosystem on exd-core (platform-deterministic PCG32 RNG)
Deterministic batch protocol (sample_batch/update_batch) shared by all algorithms
Business Source License 1.1 (free for personal/educational/research/internal use)
body:
Optimization turns engineering judgment loops into automated search. Extropian Optimization is a domain-independent C++ library built around a modular optimizer core and a batch execution protocol (`sample_batch`/`update_batch`). It ships five pluggable algorithms — CMA-ES (flagship, active covariance + IPOP restarts), NSGA-II for multi-objective Pareto fronts, deterministic Nelder-Mead and Hooke-Jeeves for low-dimension polish, and differential evolution for coarse global search.

Runs are deterministic by contract: the same seed yields a bit-for-bit identical trajectory regardless of thread count, with candidates generated before evaluation and consumed in index order. A thread pool handles parallel batch evaluation, while an embedded stepper mode hands control to hosts that own their evaluation pipeline — such as a simulator's frame-batched solver pools — with bit-identical results to one-shot runs.

Problems are expressed via a `[0,1]^d` design space mapped to engineering units (continuous, integer, categorical), with adaptive penalty and constrained domination for constraints, budgets/plateau/wall-clock stopping, JSON-defined problems for runtime configuration, and result history including multi-objective Pareto archives.

title: Extropian Core
description: The foundational C++23 platform library of the ecosystem — math, a sparse-set ECS, SceneGraph and transforms, and core utilities that every Extropian component builds on.
tagline: One shared C++23 foundation for the Extropian ecosystem — math, ECS, transforms, and utilities.
capabilities: Header-only GLM-style linear algebra — vectors, matrices, quaternions, dual quaternions, bounds, raycasting
Sparse-set, archetype-free ECS with entity generation counters, views, command buffers, and ordered system graphs
Generic SceneGraph hierarchy with LocalTransform/WorldTransform derived by TransformSystem
Core utilities: config with TOML I/O, thread-safe logging, bump allocators, serialization, event bus, plugin loader, abstract WindowState input
JSON-serializable authored document schemas (VisualDocument, StyleProfile, semantic input, UI presentation state)
foundation: C++23 and the C++ standard library — no runtime dependencies, compiles to WASM with zero changes
No GPU abstraction lives in core; GPU, audio, windowing, and app logic are explicit non-goals
Consumed as the shared foundation by render, spatial-ui, CAE, geometry, and app
body:
Extropian Core is the lowest-level shared infrastructure for the entire Extropian ecosystem. Every other Extropian library — render, spatial-ui, CAE, geometry, app — depends on it, and it in turn depends on nothing beyond C++23 and the standard library. It provides `exd::math` (templated Vec2–Vec4, Mat3/Mat4, Quat, DualQuat, Bounds3, Raycast, Color, all header-only), the `exd::ecs` framework (Entity, Registry, sparse-set component storage, Views, CommandBuffer, SystemGraph, ISystem), and `exd::core` utilities (config, logging, units, allocators, serialization, event bus, plugin loader, and an abstract WindowState input interface).

Architecturally the ecosystem converged on one spine hosted here: entities and components are common state, a generic `exd::ecs::SceneGraph` is the only hierarchy model, and transforms are component state — `LocalTransform` plus `WorldTransform` derived each update by `TransformSystem`. UI, CAE, and render semantics are carried as components rather than graph features, so one ECS and one SceneGraph serve spatial 2.5D UI, multiphysics scenes, and rendering alike. Core deliberately does not own GPU resources, audio, window creation, or application logic.

Extropian Core also owns the cross-language schema structs in `exd::types` (the authored `VisualDocument`, `StyleProfile`, semantic input, runtime UI `PresentationState`, and patch types) with C++ as the single authority. It ships as a static library (`exd::core`), integrates via CMake FetchContent, and compiles to WASM with zero changes.

title: Extropian MCP
description: The MCP agent host for the Extropian ecosystem — an AI agent that drives LLM providers and acts on whatever Extropian repos are registered as tools, with conversational state and hooks.
tagline: An AI agent host that drives LLMs with tool access across the Extropian ecosystem.
capabilities: Drives LLM providers (Ollama / OpenCode) with JSON-mediated tool calls
Tool registry over registered Extropian repos, loaded from each repo's prompts/ folder
Conversational state management — Q&A turns, history budgeting, reproducible snapshots
Hooks so an embedding host can load conversation state into spatial-ui widgets
MCP-shaped tool definitions ready for future tools/list and tools/call server adapters
foundation: Built on extropian-core shared types as the schema authority
Per-repo prompts-folder convention: each registered repo teaches the AI how to use its tools
Provider abstraction for local (Ollama) and code-agent (OpenCode) LLM backends
body:
Extropian MCP is the agent host of the Extropian ecosystem: an AI agent that drives LLM providers (Ollama / OpenCode) and acts on the ecosystem by calling whichever repos are registered as tools — spatial-ui, geometry, assets, physics, optimization, and others. It also manages conversational state (Q&A turns, history budgeting) with hooks so an embedding host can load that state into widgets, plus optional voice support via hooks.

Registered repos each ship a `prompts/` folder whose files teach the AI how to use that repo's tools — extropian-mcp loads them at runtime, with no embedded prompts. Tool definitions are MCP-shaped (name, description, input JSON Schema), so a future MCP-server adapter over the registry maps one-to-one onto `tools/list` / `tools/call`.

"MCP" names the product category, not protocol conformance: extropian-mcp is the agent-runtime library that an Extropian host embeds; it does not (yet) speak the MCP JSON-RPC protocol. Server and client adapters are planned. The current version (v0.3) was rebuilt as the generic agent host after the visual-document-specific machinery moved to extropian-spatial-ui, and ships with a passing test suite.

title: Extropian Voice
description: The audio layer of the Extropian stack — microphone capture, voice activity detection, speech-to-text, and text-to-speech for desktop and browser.
tagline: Capture, transcribe, and synthesize speech — one audio library for desktop and browser.
capabilities: Microphone capture and speaker playback with pluggable audio backends (SDL3 native, Web Audio API in-browser)
Real-time voice activity detection from raw PCM with speech/energy signals
Speech-to-text via local Whisper or cloud Deepgram/OpenAI providers
Text-to-speech via local Piper or cloud ElevenLabs/OpenAI providers
End-to-end voice pipeline wiring capture → VAD → transcribe → synthesize → playback
foundation: C++23 static library with extropian-core Signal<T> eventing
Platform-agnostic shared core (compiles to WASM) over SDL3 / Web Audio API backends
Provider abstraction layer supporting local (Whisper, Piper) and cloud (Deepgram, ElevenLabs, OpenAI) engines
body:
Engineering software should listen as well as it shows. Extropian Voice is the audio layer of the Extropian dependency stack: it owns microphone capture, speaker playback, voice activity detection, speech-to-text transcription, and text-to-speech synthesis, wired together through a `VoiceService` state machine (Idle → Listening → UserSpeaking → Processing → Speaking → Interrupted). It is deliberately low-level — conversation turn-taking, transcript routing, and UI live in other Extropian components, not here.

The core compiles unchanged for both native and WASM. Platform I/O is dispatched behind `AudioCapture`/`AudioPlayback` interfaces — SDL3 on desktop, Web Audio API via Emscripten in the browser. Speech-to-text and text-to-speech go through provider abstractions: local Whisper (whisper.cpp) and Piper TTS on desktop, and cloud Deepgram/ElevenLabs/OpenAI over HTTP.

It is built on extropian-core's `Signal<T>` event system and builds as a static library with optional provider backends toggled at configure time.

title: Extropian App
description: The desktop application shell for Extropian — SDL3 window, OpenGL 4.6 context, input, and main loop exposed through the abstract core::WindowState interface.
tagline: The desktop application shell for Extropian — SDL3 windows, OpenGL context, input, and main loop.
capabilities: SDL3 window creation with an OpenGL 4.6 core profile context
Per-frame keyboard, mouse, scroll, and gamepad input snapshots
FPS vs UI input modes with normal/hidden/captured cursor control
Minimal Application lifecycle (on_startup/on_update/on_shutdown) around a main loop
Implements core::WindowState so the renderer stays SDL-free
foundation: SDL3 for windowing, GL context, input, and gamepad
OpenGL 4.6 core profile
extropian-core for the WindowState interface, math types, clock, and logging
body:
Every desktop application starts with a window and an event loop. Extropian App is the desktop platform library of the ecosystem: it creates an SDL3 window with an OpenGL 4.6 core profile context, polls input events, and exposes them through the abstract `core::WindowState` interface defined in extropian-core — so downstream systems (like the renderer) never touch SDL3 directly.

The framework is intentionally minimal: a `Window` class wraps the SDL3 window and GL context, an `EventState` captures a per-frame snapshot of keyboard, mouse, scroll, and gamepad input, and an `Application` base class provides an `on_startup` / `on_update` / `on_shutdown` lifecycle around the main loop. It depends only on extropian-core; it deliberately excludes rendering, audio, and AI orchestration, which live in other Extropian libraries.

Currently Linux-focused, with SDL3 providing the cross-platform abstraction for Windows, macOS, and mobile.
